title: Molecular representations and physical prediction
summary: I study what learned states retain and when they help physical prediction. CG polymer and MACE water explorations led to controlled-response tests and current work on pretrained-feature transfer and label efficiency.
question: Which physical information survives representation learning, and when does it improve prediction beyond matched baselines?
progression: CG and MACE JEPA → controlled-response tests and pretrained-feature transfer
cvSummary: From CG polymer and MACE water explorations to controlled physical-response tests and current pretrained-feature transfer studies; each task has its own physical targets and evidence limits.

stages.label: Current direction
stages.context: This branch asks when pretrained atomistic features help property prediction. Completed QM9 comparisons and a crystal extension in preparation address static properties, separately from earlier dynamical tasks.

stages.label: Recent completed study
stages.context: This synthetic-system investigation follows the earlier CG and MACE representation questions into controlled physical response. It tests state use and physical readouts without claiming a molecular or real-material result.

stages.label: Earlier exploration · closed
stages.context: This atomistic-water phase followed the CG encoder comparison and closed on 9 October 2026. Its limits informed later response and transfer questions; it is no longer an ongoing water study.

stages.label: Earlier exploration · completed
stages.context: The original CG polymer study examined geometric interfaces, physical readouts, and temporal learning. It motivated the subsequent MACE encoder comparison and broader questions about physically useful representations.

title: MLIP material properties and efficiency
summary: I develop polymer-property workflows and examine their computational cost. Current density work connects classical preparation, MACE sampling, and reference comparisons; earlier resource studies grew from GPU-memory limits encountered with UMA / FAIR-Chem.
question: How can ML interatomic potentials support credible material-property calculations within practical compute and memory budgets?
progression: UMA / FAIR-Chem exploration → MACE property simulations → GPU resource evaluation
cvSummary: Ongoing polymer-density workflow development, supported by earlier MACE resource measurements and the UMA / FAIR-Chem exploration that motivated my interest in MLIP efficiency.

stages.label: Current workflow development
stages.context: This ongoing branch connects classical polymer preparation, MACE density sampling, and reference comparisons. The numerical figure is a dated September pilot; expanding the workflow does not itself establish broader accuracy.

stages.label: Earlier engineering measurements
stages.context: This engineering pilot examines the computational cost of MACE molecular dynamics. It develops the resource-efficiency question raised by the earlier UMA memory constraints, without claiming a new optimization algorithm.

stages.label: Earlier exploration and motivation
stages.context: This resource-limited exploration is the starting point of the MLIP property-calculation line. Memory constraints prevented validated UMA property results and motivated the later focus on computational efficiency.
